paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Circuit-Based Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Portfolio Optimization

summary: This paper studies dynamic portfolio optimization with two gate-based quantum reinforcement learning models: a quantum DDPG and a quantum DQN, both using variational quantum circuits with amplitude encoding and 30 or 60 trainable parameters. On 7-fold expanding-window cross-validation, the best classical DQN reaches a Sharpe ratio of 0.8237 and the best classical DDPG 0.7926, while the quantum models reach 0.7281 (QDDPG, 60 params) and 0.6537 (QDQN, 60 params); quantum inference on IBM Eagle r3 is reported with 10,000 shots and cloud job durations of 23 and 43 minutes, respectively.

experiments.description: Quantum DDPG for dynamic portfolio optimization using a variational quantum circuit actor-critic architecture, trained on historical market data and evaluated against classical baselines; trained on a noiseless statevector simulator and deployed for inference on IBM Eagle r3 superconducting hardware.

algorithm.variant: fully quantum DDPG with VQC actor and VQC critic
algorithm.ansatz: amplitude-encoded feature map followed by alternating layers of parameterized single-qubit rotations and entangling gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical financial observations are normalized, expanded with feature map Z(x)=[x, x^2, sin(x), cos(x)], then amplitude-encoded; first N qubits are measured to obtain N asset weights, followed by l1 normalization
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize risk-adjusted portfolio performance over time; reward rt = w_t^T mu_{t-L:t+F+1} - eta w_t^T Sigma_{t-L:t+F+1} w_t
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Portfolio weights are l1-normalized to sum to 1; short positions allowed; transaction costs included in evaluation

problem_instance.description: Dynamic portfolio optimization over 15 assets with 30-day lookback and 7-day forecast, rebalanced every 30 days

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily closing prices; returns computed as logarithmic differences; normalized prices; 30-day rolling window; 7-day Auto ARIMA forecast
dataset_specification.train_test_split: 7-fold expanding-window time-series cross-validation with train/validation/test splits

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log returns from daily closing prices; normalized asset prices; Auto ARIMA forecast for 7 days; expanding-window cross-validation; transaction cost of 0.15% per trade in evaluation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean and standard deviation of Sharpe ratio across 7 expanding-window cross-validation folds; final QPU inference measured with 10,000 shots

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam/SGD for training; classical baselines include equal-weight, MVO, DDPG, DQN
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical price normalization, feature-map construction, Auto ARIMA forecasting, replay buffer, Bayesian hyperparameter search
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Pauli-Z expectation values converted to portfolio weights via l1 normalization; Sharpe ratio computed on test folds
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 23 minutes cloud job duration for quantum DDPG inference deployment
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: < 1 s per circuit execution; 10,000-shot inference on QPU

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper claims practical competitiveness and better performance relative to parameter count, but no asymptotic or proven quantum speedup is shown.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports 30 trainable parameters for the quantum DDPG model, 10,000 shots for QPU inference, and deployment on IBM Eagle r3; however, no asymptotic speedup or crossover analysis is provided.
limiting_factors: Classical DDPG with 160k parameters achieves a higher Sharpe ratio (0.7926) than quantum DDPG with 30 params (0.4179) and 60 params (0.7281)
End-to-end cloud latency is 23 minutes for the quantum DDPG deployment
No proven quantum speedup is claimed; the paper emphasizes practical competitiveness rather than advantage

notes: num_qubits not explicitly stated for the VQC; inferred as at least 15 measured qubits from the 15-asset action vector, but exact register size is not reported.
circuit_depth not reported; only that the model uses alternating layers of rotations and entangling gates.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper claims practical competitiveness but no asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper's Table 5.1 shows classical DDPG with 160k params outperforming quantum DDPG on Sharpe ratio.
The quantum model is run on a superconducting QPU, but only inference is deployed there; training is on a noiseless simulator.
